title: Elementary devissage preserves admissible module-flattening data
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, $f:X\to S$ a quasi-compact morphism locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and $\mathcal F$ a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Let $U\subset S$ be a quasi-compact open on which $\mathcal F$ is finitely presented and flat over $U$. For every $x\in\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$, $s=f(x)$, put $n=\dim_x\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$ [def-kun-dimension], where support is the locus of nonzero stalks and $\mathcal F_s$ is the pullback to $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. There are affine pointed etale neighbourhoods $g:(X_1,x_1)\to(X,x)$ and $e:(T,t)\to(S,s)$, with $e$ quasi-compact, and $f_1:X_1\to T$ satisfying $fg=ef_1$. There are affine $T$-schemes $Z,Y$, a finitely presented closed immersion $i:Z\to X_1$, a finite $T$-morphism $\pi:Z\to Y$, and a finite-type quasi-coherent module $\mathcal G$ with $i_*\mathcal G\cong g^*\mathcal F$. The morphism $h:Y\to T$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$ with geometrically integral fibres (integral after every residue-field extension). Put $\mathcal N=\pi_*\mathcal G$ and $U_T=e^{-1}(U)$. Then $\mathcal N$ is quasi-coherent of finite type and $\mathcal N|_{Y_{U_T}}$ is finitely presented and flat over $U_T$. For every $U_T$-admissible blowup $b:T^b\to T$, the strict transform $\mathcal N^b$ is flat over $T^b$ if and only if $(g^*\mathcal F)^b$ is flat over $T^b$. These strict transforms are modules on $Y\times_TT^b$ and $X_1\times_TT^b$, respectively. Etale, smooth, finite morphisms, closed immersions and module pullback/pushforward are as in [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-module-pullback]. Schemes and quasi-compactness conventions are as in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], quasi-coherence and finite type as in [pqf-def-coherent], finite presentation of module sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], and relative flatness as in [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Admissible blowups retain their finite-type centre ideals [def-nagata-admissible-blowup], and all module strict transforms use those specified ideals [def-trf-module-strict-transform].

source.place: Tag 0815, theorem-flatten-module, proof paragraph 2: the finite-presentation and relative-flatness checks and transfer through elementary devissage; Tag 057S, lemma-elementary-devissage.

proof.text: Local finite presentation implies local finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: for every affine open V of S and every affine open of f^{-1}V the ring map is finitely presented (Stacks 01TQ), hence finitely generated after forgetting the finitely many relations. Apply elementary module devissage at the specified x. Write its affine schemes as X_1,Z,Y,T and retain its module G, maps g,e,i,pi,h and all distinguished points. This gives the asserted diagram, i_*G = g^*F and the smooth relative-dimension-n geometrically integral fibres. Because T is affine and S is quasi-separated, e:T -> S is quasi-compact by qcqs morphism permanence. Hence U_T is quasi-compact: it is the inverse image of the quasi-compact open U under e.

source.place: Tags 057S, lemma-elementary-devissage; 0815, theorem-flatten-module, second paragraph; Schemes Tags 03GI and 01K4

proof.text: Apply the finite-presentation devissage lemma to these same data, including its retained singleton fibre and purely transcendental residue extension: f is locally of finite presentation, so pi is of finite presentation. Only this morphism assertion is used here; the lemma's neighbourhood assertions at the distinguished point are not assertions on the whole inverse image of U. Both i and pi are affine: i by the affine description of closed immersions, pi by the definition of a finite morphism.

Put H=g^*F=i_*G and N=pi_*G. Affine pushforward makes N quasi-coherent. To check finite type, write Y=Spec B, Z=Spec C and M=G(Z). The affine finite-type criterion makes M finite over C. Since pi is finite, C has finitely many B-generators c_j. If m_k generate M over C, the elements c_j m_k generate M over B: expand each coefficient of a C-linear combination in the c_j. N(Y) is this same M with restricted scalars, so the affine criterion makes N finite type. This also includes the zero module.

source.place: Tag 05B3, lemma-finite-over-finite-module, affine argument; Properties Tag 01PB

proof.text: On X_{1,U_T}, H is finitely presented: it is the tensor pullback of F|_{X_U}, using fg=ef_1 and composition of module pullbacks. It is quasi-coherent by pullback. For an affine open V=Spec B in X_{1,U_T}, the closed inverse image i^{-1}V=Spec C has C=B/J and G(i^{-1}V)=H(V)=M with scalar restriction. The affine criterion makes M finitely presented over B; the finitely-presented-over-subring lemma, applied to the finite-type quotient algebra B -> C, makes it finitely presented over C. These opens cover Z_{U_T}, so G|_{Z_{U_T}} is finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 0815, second paragraph; Modules Tag 01BQ; Properties Tag 01PC; Algebra Tag 0561, lemma-finitely-presented-over-subring

proof.text: Now work on any affine open V=Spec B of Y_{U_T}. Its inverse image under pi is affine, say Spec C. The finite-presentation morphism pi is locally of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], so the ring map B -> C is finitely presented by the affine-opens characterization of local finite presentation (Stacks 01TQ), and it is finite by the definition of a finite morphism; and G(pi^{-1}V) is finitely presented over C by the previous step and the affine criterion. Apply finite-extension module finite presentation to B -> C: this same module is finitely presented over B. Since N(V)=G(pi^{-1}V), the affine criterion proves N|_{Y_{U_T}} finitely presented. Thus finite presentation is checked everywhere over U_T, without assuming singleton fibres at other points.

source.place: Tag 05B4, lemma-finite-finitely-presented-module, affine proof using Algebra Tag 0564 and Properties Tag 01PC

proof.text: At every a in X_{1,U_T}, g is flat because it is etale. The source-flat pullback criterion applied to g over U shows that H_a is flat over O_{U,fg(a)}. Apply the etale local-ring flatness equivalence to e at f_1(a), with the module H_a: it is flat over O_{U_T,f_1(a)}. Hence H is flat over U_T. At z in Z_{U_T}, the closed-pushforward stalk isomorphism H_{i(z)}=G_z respects the base action, so G is flat over U_T as well.

source.place: Tag 05BA, lemma-etale-flat-up-down-local-ring; Morphisms Tag 02JZ; Sheaves Tag 00AE

proof.text: For any affine open W=Spec R in U_T, the schemes Z_W and Y_W are affine. Indeed all of Z,Y,T are affine, hence their structure maps are affine, and inverse images of affine opens under an affine morphism are affine. The affine-chart relative-flatness criterion for G on Z_W says G(Z_W) is R-flat. The pushforward N on Y_W has exactly the same R-module of sections, N(Y_W)=G(Z_W); the two R-actions coincide because pi is a T-map. Apply the criterion on Y_W to obtain N flat over W. These W cover U_T, proving the remaining flatness assertion.

Fix any specified U_T-admissible blowup b:T^b -> T, retaining its finite-type centre ideal I. Write i_b and pi_b for the base changes and G^b for the strict transform of G with this same I. Strict-transform affine pushforward gives (i_*G)^b = i_{b,*}G^b and N^b = pi_{b,*}G^b. The first is H^b since i_*G=H: pullback takes this isomorphism to an isomorphism identifying the subsheaves of sections vanishing off the same exceptional closed subset, hence also their quotients. The strict-transform sheaf-kernel lemma makes G^b quasi-coherent, and affine pushforward makes both displayed pushforwards quasi-coherent. No centre is replaced by the complement of U_T.

source.place: Tags 080G, lemma-strict-transform-affine, and 080D, definition-strict-transform and preceding paragraph

proof.text: For any affine open W=Spec R in T^b, put Z_W=Z times_T W, Y_W=Y times_T W, and X_W=X_1 times_T W. The three structure maps to T are affine by the affine-schemes lemma; their base changes to T^b remain affine. Consequently Z_W,Y_W,X_W are affine. On these schemes the three section modules G^b(Z_W), (pi_{b,*}G^b)(Y_W), and (i_{b,*}G^b)(X_W) are the same R-module, by the definition of pushforward and commutativity over T^b. The affine-chart flatness criterion therefore gives equivalence of their relative flatness over W. Using the two isomorphisms in step 8, this is N^b flat over W if and only if H^b flat over W. As W ranges over an affine cover of T^b, these pointwise conditions give precisely the claimed global equivalence. No singleton-fibre assertion after blowup, or flatness of b, is used.
